---
title: "Server Tutorial"
subtitle: "From an empty working directory to a query over HTTP, an asynchronous job, and the equivalent command line"
lang: en-US
---

This tutorial starts the server, creates a dataset, indexes documents, searches them, and
executes an asynchronous job. It assumes a local copy of this repository.
`SimilaritySearchServer` is the package in `server/`, and the engine it uses is the package at
the root, whose tutorial is [Getting started](../tutorials/getting-started.qmd).

Every operation below is performed over HTTP or from a command line, and none of them is
implemented in this package: each endpoint translates one engine call. Reading both tutorials
together shows which part performs each operation.

Julia 1.12 or later is required.

## Step 1: Set up the environment

The server uses the engine from this repository, so the engine is added by path once:

```bash
julia --project=server -e 'using Pkg; Pkg.develop(path="."); Pkg.instantiate()'
```

## Step 2: Start the server

```bash
julia --project=server -t auto -m SimilaritySearchServer serve
```

On its first execution, the server writes a default configuration and accepts connections on
`http://127.0.0.1:8080`. Every dataset is stored under `<workdir>/datasets/`, and the server
opens all of them when it starts, so a restart preserves their contents.

The three applications (`similarity-search`, `similarity-search-admin`,
`similarity-search-serve`) can be installed into `~/.julia/bin`, so that Julia does not have to
be invoked explicitly:

```bash
julia -e 'using Pkg; Pkg.Apps.develop(path="server")'
```

## Step 3: Create a dataset and index documents

```bash
curl -s -X POST localhost:8080/api/v1/datasets \
     -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
     -d '{"id": "demo", "index_kind": "bm25_invfile"}'

curl -s -X POST localhost:8080/api/v1/datasets/demo/append \
     -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
     -d '{"items": [
           {"doc_id": "d1", "text": "el gato duerme sobre el tejado", "keywords": ["gato"]},
           {"doc_id": "d2", "text": "un perro ladra en la calle", "year": 2024}
         ]}'
```

`index_kind` names the type of data the project holds and the structure that indexes it:
`searchgraph` for dense vectors, which is the default; `bm25_invfile` or `invfile` for text;
and `sparse_invfile` for sparse vectors encoded by the caller, which also requires `dimension`.
Any field other than `doc_id`, `keywords`, `refs`, `text`, `vector`, `indices` and `values`
becomes metadata of the item, such as `year` in the example above.

The insertion indexes the documents, so they can be searched when the call returns.

## Step 4: Search

```bash
curl -s -X POST localhost:8080/api/v1/datasets/demo/ftsearch \
     -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
     -d '{"text": "gato tejado", "k": 5}'
```

A dense project uses `/api/v1/datasets/{id}/search`, which receives a `vector` and accepts a
metadata `filter`:

```json
{"vector": [0.1, 0.2, 0.3], "k": 10, "filter": {"year": {"$gte": 2024}}}
```

A filtered search reads a limited number of candidates before applying the filter, so it can
return fewer than `k` results. The response reports this condition in the field
`insufficient_results`.

## Step 5: Read failures

Failures are typed, and the status code identifies the class of the failure without the message
being read:

| status | meaning | example |
| ---: | :--- | :--- |
| 400 | the request cannot be executed as written | a dense `vector` sent to a text project |
| 404 | an object named in the request does not exist | an unknown dataset identifier |
| 409 | the project is not in a state that allows the request | a job over the entire dataset while items are staged |
| 500 | the stored data could not be read | — |

The body contains `error`, the message, and `kind`, the concrete error type of the engine, so
that a client can select a behavior from `kind` without comparing text.

## Step 6: Run a heavy job

An operation that reads the entire collection is executed as a job. The HTTP call enqueues the
job and returns immediately, and a dispatcher executes it in a separate Julia subprocess.

```bash
JOB=$(curl -s -X POST localhost:8080/api/v1/jobs/allknn \
      -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
      -d '{"dataset": "demo", "k": 5}' | jq -r .job_id)

curl -s localhost:8080/api/v1/jobs/$JOB          # queued | running | completed | failed
curl -s localhost:8080/api/v1/jobs/$JOB/result   # once completed
```

A job opens its dataset in read-only mode, so it can run while the server continues to answer
queries on that dataset.

## Step 7: The same thing from the command line

Every operation is also available as a subcommand, applied to a working directory instead of a
URL:

```bash
julia --project=server -m SimilaritySearchServer build \
      --dataset demo_cli --input corpus.jsonl --index-kind bm25_invfile --workdir ./workdir

julia --project=server -m SimilaritySearchServer describe --dataset demo_cli --workdir ./workdir
```

The exit codes of the command line correspond to the status codes above: `2` for an invalid
request, `4` for an object that does not exist, `5` for a conflicting state, and `70` for a
storage failure. Code `1` is reserved for failures detected by the command itself, such as a
dataset that does not exist or an input file that cannot be read. A script can select a branch
from these codes without reading the output.

## Step 8: The Python client

```bash
cd server/python
pip install -r requirements.txt
export PYTHONPATH=$(pwd)
```

```python
from similarity_search.client import SimilaritySearchClient
from similarity_search.jobs import run_job

client = SimilaritySearchClient("http://127.0.0.1:8080")
print(client.readyz())                      # {'status': 'ok'}

ds_id = client.create_dataset()
result = run_job(client, kind="allknn", command=["--dataset", ds_id, "--k", "5"])
```

`stress_client.py` executes the same sequence under concurrent load:

```bash
python stress_client.py --jobs 3
```

## Step 9: Require a token

Everything above answered without credentials, which is the default. To require a token on
every `/api/v1` endpoint, create the first token against the working directory and enable
authentication:

```bash
similarity-search add-token --user admin --permissions "admin:*" --workdir ./workdir
```

```toml
[auth]
enabled = true
```

The command prints the token once. A server started with `enabled = true` and no token
refuses to start, because no request could be answered. From then on, each request carries it:

```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
     -X POST localhost:8080/api/v1/datasets/demo/ftsearch \
     -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
     -d '{"text": "gato tejado", "k": 5}'
```

A permission is `operation:dataset`, with `read`, `write` or `admin` as the operation and a
dataset id or `*` as the scope. A token for an ingestion process is
`--permissions "write:demo"`, which also reads `demo` and reaches nothing else. `/healthz`,
`/readyz` and `/metrics` keep answering without a token. See the
[server manual](manual.qmd#authentication) for the complete table.
